reasoning: The claim that Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short and around 5 feet 2 inches tall is false. While contemporary French records (including his autopsy) measured Napoleon at "5 pieds 2 pouces" (5 feet 2 inches in French pre-metric units), the French inch (*pouce*) was longer than the English inch. When converted to modern English/international measurements, his height was approximately 5 feet 6 inches (about 1.67 meters). During the early 19th century, the average height of a French man was roughly 5 feet 5 inches, meaning Napoleon was actually of average or slightly above-average height for his era. The myth of his extreme shortness was perpetuated by a combination of the measurement conversion confusion, British wartime propaganda (notably caricature art by James Gillray), and the fact that he was often surrounded by his elite Imperial Guard who were exceptionally tall.
